newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung Display sees '97 earnings flat.
newsitem.headline: Samsung Display sees '97 earnings flat.

text.p: Earnings of South Korea's Samsung Display Devices Co Ltd are expected to be flat this year due to weak prices of colour display tubes for computer monitors, the chief executive officer said on Wednesday.
Samsung, a unit of Samsung Group, registered a net profit of 164.2 billion won last year.
"We see our 1997 net profit unchanged from last year's level because of a fall in colour display tube prices," Sun Wook, president and CEO of Samsung Display, told Reuters in an interview.
Sun said international prices of the once popular 14-inch colour display tubes have dropped 30 percent since the second half of 1996.
"The decline in tube prices has forced the industry to cut production," he said.

Samsung, the world's largest maker of colour picture and display tubes, was among the first tube makers to curtail production when it reduced its output of 14-inch colour display tubes by 30 percent in March.
Currently, Samsung is operating at 90 percent of capacity, he said.
"We plan to resume full production in August to meet the expected rising demand towards the year-end," said Sun.
He said his company had no plans to cut production in the future unless there was a drastic drop in prices.
"We have decided to partially delay new overseas projects instead," he said.
Sun said plans for additional lines for colour display tubes in Brazil and a new plant in Europe have been postponed.
Samsung Display now has overseas plants in Malaysia, Germany and Mexico. It has factories under construction in Shenzhen and Tianjin in China and in Manaus, Brazil.
Other plants are under consideration in the Commonwealth of Independent States, India and Europe, he said.
Sun said he hoped to raise the overseas tube production ratio to 57 percent by 2000 from the current 39 percent.
He said Samsung Display saw its sales rising to 2.7 trillion in 1997 from 2.46 trillion in 1996.
